name: Titanic
hook: The 1912 liner that made "unsinkable" a cautionary word, and the 1997 film that made it a blockbuster.

facts.label: April 1912
facts.statement: The Titanic sank on its maiden voyage, striking an iceberg at 11:40 p.m. on April 14, 1912 and going under about 2:20 a.m. on April 15.

facts.label: unsinkable
facts.statement: It was widely billed as unsinkable, a boast that became a byword for hubris. Violet Jessop survived the sinking of the Titanic and the Britannic, and was aboard the Olympic when it collided with HMS Hawke in 1911.

facts.label: Belfast
facts.statement: It was built in Belfast, Northern Ireland, by Harland & Wolff and owned by the White Star Line, which in turn belonged to J.P. Morgan.

facts.label: the Carpathia
facts.statement: The Cunard liner Carpathia raced to the scene and had rescued about 705 survivors from the lifeboats by 9 a.m. on April 15.

facts.label: Molly Brown
facts.statement: Margaret "Molly" Brown was a survivor later called the Unsinkable Molly Brown; she presented the Carpathia's captain with a silver loving cup.

facts.label: James Cameron's 1997 film
facts.statement: James Cameron's 1997 film starred Leonardo DiCaprio and Kate Winslet as Jack and Rose, and Celine Dion sang "My Heart Will Go On."
